summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and history of GERD and prior GJ ulcer presented with 1.5 weeks of persistent nausea, epigastric pain, dry heaves, and poor oral intake with concern for malnutrition. She was treated with IV fluids including vitamin supplementation, IV antiemetics/analgesia, sucralfate, and IV pantoprazole; Nutrition evaluated her as at risk for malnutrition. On hospital day 2 a left PICC was placed and TPN was initiated and gradually advanced to goal without evidence of refeeding syndrome, then transitioned to a nocturnal cycle in preparation for discharge. On hospital day 5 she underwent EGD, which showed mild gastritis and a small hiatal hernia; GI recommended increasing pantoprazole to 80 mg IV twice daily and suggested outpatient evaluation for possible cyclic vomiting syndrome. She improved clinically with resolution of dry heaves and nausea, improved epigastric pain, and tolerance of small amounts of stage 5 bariatric diet, and was discharged home with services on nocturnal TPN and high-dose IV pantoprazole with planned outpatient lab monitoring and GI/surgical follow-up.
